beta_new: Begin as for the neighboring Giz Gaz and take the left one of a pair of matching flake cracks through the bulge; on the second pitch you ascend the block above while clipping a pin and a few bolts.
Bolts lead up to a lengthy roof; work leftward past more bolts to get around its left end, then keep going up the wall above it.
About 500 feet of climbing gains a broad ledge; shift right, then go up and slightly right, clipping three bolts on the way to the ceilings. Easier ground then eases toward the slabs below the top.
Stay on the arete standing to the left of a clean corner that faces right; higher up, step off it to the left. A single bolt sits at the start.
Stay on the Egghead line until just beyond its second bolt, then drift five feet right and go directly up.
The route is a sustained, technical pumper from the first clip to the anchor, and some climbers rate it harder than its number suggests.
Cross leftward along ledges from the crag's right end, tackle the overhang by its two bolts, then angle up and leftward past one more bolt to meet Sidewinder for that route's closing traverse.
Keep an eye out for bolt number four: it blends in with the rock and is set well to the right.
Protect the crack under the second bolt with gear in the 2 to 3 inch range, in addition to the bolts.

moves.from: Protect the crack under the second bolt with gear in the 2 to 3 inch range, in addition to the bolts.

value.text: Gear in the 2 to 3 in range for the crack under the second bolt.

beta_new: Work up the deep scoops close to the crag's left margin, clipping three bolts.

moves.from: Supplement the bolts with large nuts, sizes 4 to 5, and slings tied off around knobs.

value.text: Large nuts in sizes 4 to 5, plus slings to tie off around knobs.

beta_new: Most parties stop after the first pitch, where the crack thins and you are pushed left to reach a far-off edge.

moves.from: Gear to about 2 inches works, especially very small pieces under 1 inch.

rows.sizes: to about 2 in, especially pieces under 1 in

beta_new: Placing protection is tricky for a typical leader at this standard.
Follow the brown dike as it slants leftward, passing three bolts that have chain-link hangers, and then continue by a fixed pin.
Layback a slim flake leaning to the right, clipping two bolts, then continue upward until reaching the final bolt of Sexy Sady.
Clip two bolts and then ascend the thin crack above.
The anchor is partly concealed, roughly 40 ft over the final bolt and a touch right, beneath the overhang. Shorter climbers will find the moves harder.
Three bolts protect it, the last one set high toward the face's upper right corner, off to the right of the following route's upper part.
Begin by traversing rightward from the neighboring route's start, then climb past three bolts and step left at the last one. The first bolt is a long way up.
Clip three bolts, then step left into Czech Cows Say Boo's upper crack.
Follow the prominent water chute up the back of the formation. The rock gets a little better to the left once past the third bolt, where the crux is.
Start on holes slanting leftward past one bolt, then pull up a corner that leans left and crosses an overhang to reach a ledge. From there continue up the second pitch or leave rightward.
Use the bucket holds trending rightward to the first bolt, then angle left past three further bolts to the top.
Begin at a bolt immediately right of the previous route, then trend rightward, keeping near the arete on the formation's right side.
The first pitch is strenuous free climbing on the ladder of old aid bolts.

From a ledge slanting up and left beneath the highest trees, climb two corners up to a block, then pass a bolt plus the crux to reach a second bolt. Go up-left, then up-right until a fixed pin appears.

Traverse straight left, then work back up rightward, arriving at a horizontal crack. Hard mantle and face moves lead beyond a third bolt onto a two-pin stance. One easier pitch finishes it.
Pass the first bolt shared with Racing Stripes, then exit up and rightward onto the overhanging headwall beside the crack; the steep, dynamic moves up there are the payoff.
Move up the face, clipping four bolts, and stay with the faint dark streak.
Begin beside a juniper and climb flakes facing left up to a ramp, then pass a bolt (which may no longer be there) en route to the finish.

Start from ledges on the face's left side and climb rightward into a crack within an open book; two flakes beneath the corner give harder direct starts. Follow the corner up to a big bolted ledge, then step left into a second corner and finish via a short face with one bolt.
Start by the detached flake at the base, follow the straight-in crack, and expect to work over a bulge close to the top.

Begin beside a bush, working a slender left-facing flake up under a small roof, then continue beyond two bolts onto a belay ledge. Pitch two follows either the crack overhead or the face on its right, which has one bolt (perhaps two).
Begin from the ledge atop the preceding four routes and traverse leftward the full width of the face; you will clip a bolt that belongs to the neighboring Rap Bolters line.
Nine bolts lead to a belay on a horizontal ledge; from there step left and finish on the route sharing that belay, or bail left to the anchors above Stemski.
Follow cracks up the small rock; a bolt sits a little way below the summit.
Start where the previous route ends, climb a dihedral that has a bolt, then angle up and rightward past a second one plus a horizontal crack to the top.
After clipping the fourth bolt, head rightward around the arete and finish upward.
Do the crux section borrowed from Hidden Arch, then traverse rightward and ascend the easier face above, ending at the anchor Loose Lady uses.
Ascend bucket holds up the left part of the brown face, clipping a bolt and passing some bushes.
Pitch one goes past a bolt on the strip separating two neighboring routes and finishes at the anchors belonging to Grey Cell Green; pitch two moves left, clips two bolts and passes a few pins.
